objects.name: PowerShell
objects.description:
Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution. PowerShell is a powerful interactive command-line interface and scripting environment included in the Windows operating system. Adversaries can use PowerShell to perform a number of actions, including discovery of information and execution of code. Examples include the Start-Process cmdlet which can be used to run an executable and the Invoke-Command cmdlet which runs a command locally or on a remote computer (though administrator permissions are required to use PowerShell to connect to remote systems).

PowerShell may also be used to download and run executables from the Internet, which can be executed from disk or in memory without touching disk.

A number of PowerShell-based offensive testing tools are available, including Empire, PowerSploit, PoshC2, and PSAttack.

PowerShell commands/scripts can also be executed without directly invoking the powershell.exe binary through interfaces to PowerShell's underlying System.Management.Automation assembly DLL exposed through the .NET framework and Windows Common Language Interface (CLI).

title: Potential PowerShell Activity Via Process Creation

status: experimental
description: |
    Draft detection for T1059.001 (PowerShell), derived from ATT&CK detection strategy DET0455 /
    analytic AN1252.
    Adversaries may abuse PowerShell commands and scripts for execution. PowerShell is a powerful
    interactive command-line interface and scripting environment included in the Windows operating
    system.
    ATT&CK analytic: Detects behavioral chains where PowerShell is launched with encoded commands,
    unusual parent processes, or suspicious modules loaded, potentially followed by network
    connections or child process spawning. Supports detection of both direct (powershell.exe) and
    indirect (.NET automation) invocations.
    Generated draft - the selection values below were mined from ATT&CK and must be validated
    against real telemetry before this rule is deployed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001
    - https://attack.mitre.org/detectionstrategies/DET0455
    - https://attack.mitre.org/detectionstrategies/DET0455#AN1252

    - https://web.archive.org/web/20190508170150/https://silentbreaksecurity.com/powershell-jobs-without-powershell-exe/

date: 2026-09-24
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1059.001
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'

            - Invoke-Command
